newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas Q1 hurt by Delta II, costs.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas Q1 hurt by Delta II, costs.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said Thursday its earnings for the first quarter were hurt by accident-related costs and fewer launches resulting from a Delta II failure in January 1997.
It also cited increased costs on its MD-95 commercial aircraft and Delta III development programs, as well as costs related to the pending merger of McDonnell Douglas with Boeing Co.
McDonnell added that earnings for the first quarter of 1996 were increased by an environmental insurance recovery.
The amount of the year-ago insurance recovery was not disclosed.
The Delta II costs refer to a rocket, built by McDonnell Douglas, which exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida, in January.
In March, McDonnell Douglas completed another phase of testing for the Delta III. It said the first Delta III launch was set for 1998.

McDonnell Douglas said it had firm backlog of $23.4 billion on March 31, down from $23.7 billion as of December 31, 1996. Total backlog was $43.1 billion on March 31, down from $44.4 billion on December 31.

The company said its interest expense for the first quarter was $35 million, up from $31 million a year ago. The increase releated to a higher level of aerospace debt, reflecting the issuance of $250 million of 10-year notes in late 1996, it added.
McDonnell Douglas said it had $250 million of senior debt securities, which matured in early April 1997.
